title: Pennsylvania's 8th Congressional District election, 2026
description: The general election for Pennsylvania's 8th Congressional District pits freshman Republican incumbent Rob Bresnahan Jr. against Democratic challenger Paige Cognetti, the mayor of Scranton. The district covers northeastern Pennsylvania, including Scranton, Wilkes-Barre, and the Pocono region, and has a Cook Partisan Voting Index of R+4. Bresnahan flipped the seat from Democratic control in 2024 by defeating longtime incumbent Matt Cartwright, making this a key battleground as Democrats seek to retake the House majority. Bresnahan's stock trading activities have become a central campaign issue, while Cognetti emphasizes her record as Scranton's first female mayor and her anti-corruption platform.
polling_note: Only one publicly released poll was found — an early September 2025 internal poll from the Democratic-aligned House Majority PAC showing Cognetti leading Bresnahan 45% to 43%. No independent or nonpartisan polls were available as of mid-2026. The Cook Political Report moved the race rating to 'Toss Up' in April 2026.

candidates.name: Rob Bresnahan Jr.
candidates.summary: Rob Bresnahan Jr. is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Pennsylvania's 8th Congressional District, first elected in 2024 after defeating Democratic incumbent Matt Cartwright. A businessman and former CEO of Kuharchik Construction, he has been a subject of controversy due to extensive stock trading activity since taking office, which has become a central issue in his re-election campaign. He serves on the House Agriculture, Transportation and Infrastructure, and Small Business Committees.

candidates.name: Paige Cognetti
candidates.summary: Paige Cognetti is the mayor of Scranton, Pennsylvania, first elected as an independent in a 2019 special election following a corruption scandal, and re-elected as a Democrat in 2021. She is the first woman to serve as Scranton's mayor and has focused on government reform, economic development, and infrastructure investments. She launched her congressional campaign in September 2025 with an emphasis on ethics reform, targeting incumbent Rob Bresnahan's stock trading record.

forecast.rationale: This race is a genuine tossup with very sparse public polling. The only available survey is a Democratic-aligned internal poll from September 2025 — nearly a year old — showing Cognetti ahead 45%-43%, which carries limited evidentiary weight due to age and partisan sponsorship. The fundamentals cut both ways: Bresnahan is the freshman incumbent in an R+4 district, giving Republicans a modest structural edge, but the seat was held by Democrats for 12 years prior to 2024, and Cognetti is a strong, well-known challenger as Scranton's mayor with demonstrated crossover appeal (first elected as an independent). Cook Political Report's shift to Toss Up in April 2026 confirms the competitive dynamics. With only one dated, partisan-sponsored poll and mixed fundamentals, the race is too close to call, though incumbency and district partisanship provide a very narrow Republican lean.
